stemMarkdown: A vessel contains 50 litres of pure milk. 8 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated 2 times in total. How many litres of milk remain in the vessel? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Each operation leaves $\dfrac{42}{50}$ of the milk behind. After 2 operations the milk left is $50 \times \left(\dfrac{42}{50}\right)^{2} = 35.28$ litres.
altSolutionMarkdown: General rule: milk remaining $= V\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{V}\right)^n$. The water added never changes the vessel's volume, which is why the same fraction applies every round.
